shouldFix.charge: The draft states "leftover-join.v9 pins HEAD `{JOINHEAD}`, the HEAD at which both Stage A reviews measured." `{JOINHEAD}` is an unsubstituted template placeholder, not a commit identifier. As written the sentence asserts a HEAD pin that does not exist; the frozen join's top-level `head` and `recordedInputs.HEAD` are both `e4b20dd9b282c519cc85ecc4711da513d1efca10`.
shouldFix.evidence: grep -nE '\{[A-Za-z_]+\}' on the subject returns only line 61. jq '.head, .recordedInputs.HEAD' on component-manifest-leftover-join.v9.json (e71dca64…) returns e4b20dd9b282c519cc85ecc4711da513d1efca10 twice. No other draft (D-2xx) and no adopted COORD entry contains a brace placeholder.
shouldFix.whyThisMatters: This entry is adopted by append-only copy into COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md. The sentence is a custody claim about which HEAD both Stage A verdicts are bound to; a literal `{JOINHEAD}` token in the permanent record neither resolves to a commit nor matches the join's bytes. Under the project's own standard (CMLJ-V7-SF1, CMLJ-V8-SF1, CMLJ-V8-SF2: every token must resolve to exactly one artifact/value and must not be contradicted by the bytes), this is the same class of defect that produced the v7 and v8 Stage A REJECTs.
shouldFix.whyNotAMustFix: The true value appears three times elsewhere in the same draft (line 57, the first clause of line 61, and the line-101 table row), so no reader is misled about which HEAD is meant, and no authority, status, currency, or identifier claim is affected. The defect is a rendering failure in a sentence whose surrounding facts are all verified true.
shouldFix.suggestedRepairShape: Substitute the literal commit: "leftover-join.v9 pins HEAD `e4b20dd9b282c519cc85ecc4711da513d1efca10`, the HEAD at which both Stage A reviews measured." No other change implied. A regenerated draft would carry a new digest; this review is bound to 048620e1… and does not pre-approve the successor.
shouldFix.notARequestTo: Change the HEAD pin, re-measure the join, edit the frozen join, edit COORD or file 08, or alter any currency conclusion.

shouldFix.charge: The overturn label is written `C-D-282`. Every one of the 214 `Overturn:` labels in the adopted COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, and 41 of 42 such labels across the D-25x–D-28x drafts, use the form `C-DNNN` (the D-281 draft and adopted entry: `C-D281`). `C-D-282` is a nonconforming identifier form for the overturn/commit token of this decision.
shouldFix.evidence: grep -ohE 'Overturn: C-D-?[0-9]+' docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md | sed -E 's/[0-9]+$/N/' | sort | uniq -c → 214 'C-DN', 0 'C-D-N'. Same over coordinator-decisions.D-2[5-8]*.draft.md → 41 'C-DN', 1 'C-D-N' (this subject). The adopted D-281 entry also carries '- **Commit:** C-D281.' in the same form.
shouldFix.whyThisMatters: The prompt forbids inventing identifiers. The overturn/commit label is the identifier a later C-D-cycle or overturn act must cite; a one-off `C-D-282` among 214 `C-DNNN` entries would be missed by any token-exact search for `C-D282` and is exactly the ambiguity the reviewers have rejected on in this lineage (bare/nonconforming tokens, CMLJ-V7-SF1).
shouldFix.whyNotAMustFix: A human reader resolves `C-D-282` to the overturn of D-282 without ambiguity; nothing false is asserted about any row, decision, or artifact. It is a token-form defect with no authority effect.
shouldFix.suggestedRepairShape: Write `Overturn: C-D282.` to match the established form.
shouldFix.notARequestTo: Introduce a Commit line into the draft (the adopted entry supplies it) or change any other token.
